name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 partisan lean in a heavily Republican district
Incumbent Adrian Smith running with a large cash advantage
Democratic challenger raised only $55k with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's R+27 lean, Smith's incumbency and roughly 30-to-1 fundraising edge, and markets pricing him near certain re-election leave no evidence supporting a competitive race. The forecast stays at Safe R with a margin near the fundamentals baseline.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a major scandal involving Smith, would be the only plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Nebraska's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Adrian Smith has held the seat since 2007 and is running again with the advantages of incumbency, more than $1 million in cash on hand, and no outside spending against him. His Democratic opponent, Becky Stille, has raised about $55,000 and had under $15,000 on hand, with no visible outside support. Independent and third-party candidates are on the ballot but show minimal fundraising.

Prediction markets give Smith roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and no expert rating services list the race as competitive. No general-election polling exists, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Republican win in the low twenties. The race is rated Safe R with high confidence.
